## Overview

::: {.callout-warning title="Current reporting result — computationally sound, interval crosses zero"}
The corrected 2026-08-09 `reporting` fit uses the exact same 53-child identity as MED-087 and passes the automatic computational gate. The interventional indirect contrast is +0.292 blending items (89% interval −0.098 to +0.761; P>0 = 0.888), and the total is +0.748 (−0.056 to +1.560; P>0 = 0.932). Numerical agreement with MED-087 is expected from the shared fitted model and current g-formula functional; it is an implementation check, not identification evidence. The indirect interval includes zero before any session-dose shift, and power scaling flags several parameters. This remains a model-based decomposition under unresolved confounding and same-wave assumptions, not an identified causal route.
:::

MED-187 is the parent+100 **interventional-effects companion** to [MED-087](https://github.com/dseinternational/language-reading-predictors/tree/main/docs/models/lrp-rli-med-087). Both fit the same Phase-0 joint model, use letter-sound knowledge at t2 as the mediator, use the same signed-off adjustment set, and model the graded phoneme-blending score at t2. MED-087 reports the natural direct and indirect effects (NDE/NIE); MED-187 reports their randomised-interventional analogues (IDE/IIE) on the blending-item scale.

## Why the estimand changes

Sessions attended ($IS$) are affected by randomised group and are a common cause of letter sounds and blending through $IS\to L$ and $IS\to B$. This recanting-witness structure makes the cross-world natural effects formally unidentified. The interventional analogue instead draws the mediator from its arm-specific covariate-conditional distribution, so it remains well-defined without asking for the same child's mediator under incompatible treatment worlds.

**What the label does and does not buy** (#585 finding 2). A well-defined estimand is not an identified one. An interventional effect is identified in the presence of an exposure-induced mediator–outcome confounder only when that confounder is *measured* and integrated over — within its treated distribution in the outcome leg and its control distribution in the mediator leg. Sessions attended enter neither leg of this fit, so the functional computed here identifies the interventional target only under the same no-exposure-induced-confounding condition the natural version requires, and it reproduces the parent model's numbers exactly by construction. Treat the relabelling as a change of target, not as a robustness gain; latent general ability leaves both versions unidentified regardless.

That change does **not** make MED-187 a fully identified causal mediation analysis. Latent general ability still confounds the $L\to B$ relationship, mediator and outcome are measured in the same wave, and $IS$ is not represented in the fitted joint model. IDE/IIE are therefore weaker-assumption, model-based decompositions under the stated assumptions, not identified causal routes.

## Comparison with MED-087

The fitted probabilistic model and adjustment set are intentionally identical to MED-087. In the current fully parametric g-formula, both estimand classes draw $L$ from the same fitted covariate-conditional law; changing `estimand` changes the counterfactual interpretation and the row labels, not the numerical functional. MED-187's IIE should therefore agree with MED-087's NIE up to posterior-sampling and g-formula Monte Carlo error. Agreement is an implementation check; it is **not** evidence that shared dose causes no distortion. A material gap would first indicate non-comparable fits or Monte Carlo error, not a scientific dose-confounding result.

## Adjustment set

The set is inherited directly from MED-087: randomised group $G$, age $A$, baseline letter sounds $L_{t1}$, the outcome's own baseline $B_{t1}$, baseline word reading $WR_1$, hearing $HS$ and speech production $SP$, with the raw-covariate missing indicators. $WR_1$ blocks the measured fork $LS_2\leftarrow WR_1\to PA_2$; it is distinct from $B_{t1}$ in both the specification and fitted model. Phonological memory is not a common cause of letter sounds and blending and is excluded. Baseline expressive/receptive vocabulary is not required, and no treatment-non-descendant adjustment set can block the $L_2\leftarrow IS_1\to PA_2$ witness path; the correction reduces observable backdoor bias without identifying the IDE/IIE split.
